previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and homelessness was admitted for right flank pain and bacteremia. She had left a prior hospital against medical advice with a femoral line, which was removed upon arrival and treated with vancomycin for Corynebacterium bacteremia. Labs showed stable blood counts and negative repeat blood cultures. Urine culture grew E. coli, but clinical signs did not confirm active pyelonephritis. Renal ultrasound showed no stones or hydronephrosis. She reported chronic frostbite symptoms, managed with ibuprofen and Neurontin. Despite recommendations to stay for further evaluation, including transvaginal ultrasound, she left against medical advice to attend a court hearing. She was discharged home with instructions to seek care if symptoms worsened.

ultrasound was negative for perinephric inflammation.

infection, so will not administer antibiotics at this time

concern for drug-seeking behavior.

further evaluate her pain but left AMA prior to the completion 
of these studies on her last admission

primary complaint now

- One dose of Diflucan was administered

Social work found the patient a shelter, and she will leave to 
there.

Given this patient's non-compliance with therapy, it is 
difficult to provide any continous therapy. As she has been 
admitted 27 times this year, and has left twice this week, 
including once with central access in place, therapeutic
